age.label: Mother's Age
age.desc: Your current age. Age is a significant factor in determining pregnancy risk and specialized care needs.

systolicBP.label: Systolic BP
systolicBP.desc: The higher number in a blood pressure reading. It measures the pressure in your arteries when your heart beats.

diastolicBP.label: Diastolic BP
diastolicBP.desc: The lower number in a blood pressure reading. It measures the pressure in your arteries when your heart rests between beats.

bloodGlucose.label: Random Blood Sugar (RBS)
bloodGlucose.desc: Measures glucose levels in the blood at any time. High levels may indicate Gestational Diabetes.

bodyTemp.label: Body Temperature
bodyTemp.desc: Standard body temperature. Elevated temperatures (fever) can signal underlying infections.

heartRate.label: Heart Rate (HR)
heartRate.desc: Number of heartbeats per minute. Normal resting rate for adults is 60–100 beats per minute.

hemoglobin.label: Hemoglobin Level (Hb)
hemoglobin.desc: Protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. Low levels can indicate Anemia, common during pregnancy.

hba1c.label: HBA1C Level
hba1c.desc: Reflects average blood sugar levels over the past 3 months. Used to monitor long-term glucose control.

respirationRate.label: Respiration Rate (RR)
respirationRate.desc: The number of breaths you take per minute while at rest.

weight.label: Current Weight
weight.desc: Your current body weight. Steady weight gain is a key indicator of healthy fetal growth.

gravida.label: Gravida (G)
gravida.desc: GPAL Formula (G): Total pregnancies. Represents 'G' in the system. Formula: G = P + A + current pregnancy.

para.label: Para (P)
para.desc: GPAL Formula (P): Number of pregnancies that reached viability (>20 weeks).

liveBirths.label: Live Births (L)
liveBirths.desc: GPAL Formula (L): Total children born alive. Part of your obstetric summary.

abortions.label: Abortions (A)
abortions.desc: GPAL Formula (A): Number of pregnancies lost before 20 weeks (spontaneous or induced).

childDeaths.label: Child Deaths (D)
childDeaths.desc: Total number of pediatric losses after delivery.

advice.lowRisk: Continue regular prenatal checkups and maintain a healthy diet.
advice.moderateRisk: Closer monitoring required. Schedule a follow-up appointment soon to discuss these metrics with your healthcare provider.
advice.highRisk: Immediate medical attention recommended. High probability of complications detected. Please consult your obstetrician urgently.

pregnancyRisks.pageSubtitle: Personalized insights and safety guidelines for your health.
pregnancyRisks.definitionText: A high-risk pregnancy means you have a higher-than-average risk of experiencing a pregnancy complication. Some pregnancies begin as high risk, while others become high risk at some point during the pregnancy.

pregnancySymptoms.pageSubtitle: Understanding when to seek care and what to watch for.
pregnancySymptoms.emergencyText: Talk to your pregnancy care provider right away if you experience any of the following symptoms, regardless of if your pregnancy is high risk or low risk:
emergencySymptoms: Abdominal pain that doesn't go away
Swelling, redness or pain in face/limbs
pregnancySymptoms.ageRiskQuestion: At what age is a pregnancy considered high risk?
pregnancySymptoms.ageRiskAnswer: Age alone isn't a determining factor in a high-risk pregnancy. Your pregnancy care provider determines if your pregnancy is likely to have complications based on several other factors.

pregnancySymptoms.managementNote: It's important to talk to your pregnancy care provider about your risks for these complications. Ask them any questions you have. With proper monitoring and care, you and your providers may be able to reduce your risk of having these or other complications.
